```{r load-data}
Diabetes_binary_data = read.csv("~/Health Informatics Program/Fall2026/COMP4033/R Files/diabetes_binary_5050split_health_indicators_BRFSS2015.csv")
```

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# Install tidyverse package
library("tidyverse")
```

```{r}
#Print structure of dataset (tidyverse version of str command)
glimpse(Diabetes_binary_data)
```

```{r}
# List the variables of the data set/column names
names(Diabetes_binary_data)
```

```{r}
# Print the top 15 rows of data set
head(Diabetes_binary_data, n=15)
```

```{r}
#user defined function - if statement checks if the values in the diabetes_binary are equal to 1
#and if they are the function returns "yes" and the else statement returns "no" if the value of 
#diabetes_binary is NOT equal to 1
has_diabetes = function(Diabetes_binary) {
  if (Diabetes_binary == 1) {
    return("Yes")
  } else {
    return("No")
  }
}
```

```{r}
# prints the result of the has_diabetes function at the 1st row in the diabetes_binary column
print(has_diabetes(1))
```

```{r}
# dependent variable is diabetes_binary, the rest are independent variables
# selects the HighBP, HighChol, BMI, and Smoker columns to make the independent variables
diabetes_predictors = Diabetes_binary_data[, c("HighBP", "HighChol", "BMI", "Smoker")]
# selects the Diabetes_diagnosis column to make the dependent variable, named diabetes_diagnosis
diabetes_diagnosis = Diabetes_binary_data$Diabetes_binary
# combines the columns into a new dataframe called diabetes_analysis
diabetes_analysis = cbind(diabetes_predictors, diabetes_diagnosis)
head(diabetes_analysis)
```

```{r}
# omits any missing values in the dataset
Diabetes_binary_data = na.omit(Diabetes_binary_data)
nrow(Diabetes_binary_data)
```

```{r}
# identifies duplicated data in data set and then returns the number of duplicate rows
sum(duplicated(Diabetes_binary_data))
```

```{r}
# removes any duplicates in data set and returns only the ones that are distinct and displays 
# only the first few rows
Diabetes_binary_data = Diabetes_binary_data %>% distinct()
head(Diabetes_binary_data)
```

```{r}
# arranges data by descending age and displays only the first few rows
Diabetes_binary_data = Diabetes_binary_data %>% arrange(desc(Age))
head(Diabetes_binary_data)
```

```{r}
# renames columns
names(Diabetes_binary_data)[names(Diabetes_binary_data) == "Diabetes_binary"] = "Diabetes_diagnosis"
names(Diabetes_binary_data)[names(Diabetes_binary_data) == "Veggies"] = "Eats_enough_veggies"
names(Diabetes_binary_data)[names(Diabetes_binary_data) == "GenHlth"] = "General_health"
names(Diabetes_binary_data)[names(Diabetes_binary_data) == "AnyHealthcare"] = "Has_any_healthcare"
names(Diabetes_binary_data)[names(Diabetes_binary_data) == "MentHlth"] = "Mental_health"
```

```{r}
# make a new column called socioeconomic_score and it will be the result of income x education
# and displays first few rows
Diabetes_binary_data = Diabetes_binary_data %>% mutate(SocioeconomicScore = Income*Education)
head(Diabetes_binary_data)
```

```{r}
# create a training set using random number generator engine
set.seed(1234)
training_set = Diabetes_binary_data %>% sample_frac(0.80)
nrow(training_set)
```

```{r}
# Prints the summary statistics of data set
view_all = summary(Diabetes_binary_data)
print(view_all)
```

```{r}
# Finds the mean of the BMI column
BMI_mean = mean(Diabetes_binary_data$BMI)
```

```{r}
# Finds the median for the BMI column
BMI_median = median(Diabetes_binary_data$BMI)
```

```{r}
# Finds mode of the BMI column using a user-defined function
# unique(x) extracts the unique values in the BMI column
# match(x, values) matches each observation to its position in the list of distinct
# values, where values = unique(x)
# tabulate() counts how many times each distinct value occurs
# which.max() identifies the position of the highest frequency
# values[] returns the value at that position in the newly created vector
find_mode = function(x) {
  values = unique(x)
  values[which.max(tabulate(match(x, values)))]
}
# calls the find_mode function passing the BMI data from the data set and stores it in 
# a variable called "BMI_mode"
BMI_mode = find_mode(Diabetes_binary_data$BMI)
```

```{r}
# Finds range of BMI column data
BMI_range = range(Diabetes_binary_data$BMI)
```

```{r scatter-plot, fig.width=5, fig.height=4}
# Creates a scatter plot for the income and BMI column data
ggplot(Diabetes_binary_data, aes(x = Income, y = BMI)) + geom_point(size = 1, color = "coral")
```

```{r bar-graph, fig.width=5, fig.height=4}
# Creates a bar graph for the HeartDiseaseorAttack column data
ggplot(Diabetes_binary_data, aes(x = HeartDiseaseorAttack)) + geom_bar(fill = "aquamarine")
```

```{r}
# Finds the pearson correlation between Diabetes_diagnosis and BMI
BMI_corr = cor(Diabetes_binary_data$Diabetes_diagnosis, Diabetes_binary_data$BMI, method = "pearson")
```
